correctness.rationale: Enumerated every composite factorization pattern with Ω<=3: p², pq, p³, p²q and squarefree pqr. For p² and p³ the cototient p and p² cannot divide p+1 and p²+p+1 respectively; for pq, c=p+q−1>=4 cannot divide s−c=2. For p²q, p|(q+1) and q+1=kp give p(k+1)−2 | k+2; positivity forces p=2,k=2,q=3, namely n=12. For pqr, c=pq+pr+qr−p−q−r+1 > 2(p+q+r) and c would divide 2(p+q+r), impossible. Exact independent sympy totient/divisor-sigma arithmetic for composite n<=100000 with Ω<=3 finds only 12. For 56, c=32 and s=64, Ω=4. Finite check is corroborative, unrestricted proof is factorization-case exhaustion.
residual_risks: Only describes Ω<=3, not all n or even the entire Ω=4 layer; composite-prime exclusion was explicitly checked in independent finite verifier.
